article_title: Chancellor calls for 'confidence about Britain' despite 'historic high' borrowing costs

tasks.prompt: What tension is at the centre of the article?
options: The chancellor's optimistic growth message versus pressure from high borrowing costs and strained public finances
A disagreement over whether Jaguar Land Rover should manufacture cars
A plan to abolish the Budget because markets are calm
A dispute between universities over a technology fund
tasks.correct_answer: The chancellor's optimistic growth message versus pressure from high borrowing costs and strained public finances
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה מציבה זה מול זה את מסר הביטחון והצמיחה של השר ואת הלחצים התקציביים שנובעים מעלויות הלוואה גבוהות.

tasks.prompt: What did John Healey refuse to rule out before the 28 October Budget?
options: Greater devolution to regions
Tax increases
Investment in innovative northern firms
Efforts to reduce welfare costs
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הילי לא שלל העלאות מס, אף שהתחייב להיצמד להבטחה שלא להעלות מסים על אנשים עובדים.

tasks.prompt: What does “fiscal discipline” mean in the article's context?
options: Training workers for manufacturing jobs
Moving all spending decisions to local councils
Managing government spending, revenue and borrowing responsibly
Encouraging households to borrow more money
tasks.correct_answer: Managing government spending, revenue and borrowing responsibly
tasks.explanation_hebrew: fiscal discipline מתייחס לניהול אחראי של הוצאות, הכנסות וחוב ציבורי כדי לשמור על אמון ויציבות.

tasks.prompt: Why does the article connect higher borrowing costs with possible tax rises or spending cuts?
options: Higher borrowing costs increase pressure on already stretched public finances
Government debt becomes free when interest rates rise
The chancellor promised to end all public investment
Bond investors directly choose each UK tax rate
tasks.correct_answer: Higher borrowing costs increase pressure on already stretched public finances
tasks.explanation_hebrew: כאשר עלות מימון החוב עולה, נוצר לחץ נוסף על התקציב ועלול להידרש שילוב של הכנסות נוספות או קיצוץ בהוצאות.

tasks.prompt: What is the purpose of the £150m fund unveiled for northern England?
options: To compensate every JLR worker with a cash payment
To buy government bonds during market volatility
To replace the British Business Bank
To invest in innovative, fast-growing firms and help unlock private investment
tasks.correct_answer: To invest in innovative, fast-growing firms and help unlock private investment
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הקרן נועדה להשקיע בחברות חדשניות וצומחות, ובהן מיזמים שיצאו מאוניברסיטאות, ולמשוך השקעה פרטית.

tasks.prompt: What does “room for manoeuvre” mean when discussing the government's spending plans?
options: A legal requirement to spend every available pound
Flexibility or a financial buffer to respond to shocks
A new office for Treasury officials
Permission to ignore tax receipts
tasks.correct_answer: Flexibility or a financial buffer to respond to shocks
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הביטוי מציין מרחב פעולה או כרית תקציבית שמאפשרים להגיב לזעזועים בלתי צפויים.

tasks.prompt: Set out Healey's main economic promises and the pressures complicating them.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין את יעדי הצמיחה וההשקעה לצד עלויות ההלוואה, מצב התקציב, הוצאות הביטחון והחדשות מ־JLR.
expected_points: Healey called for renewed confidence in Britain
He made growth in more places a central priority
He promoted devolution, public leadership, investment, innovation and jobs
He promised to balance day-to-day spending with tax receipts
He said the government would control spending and lower welfare costs
Borrowing costs had reached an 18-year high
Higher borrowing costs put pressure on already stretched public finances
The Treasury may face multi-billion-pound gaps
Higher defence spending adds pressure
JLR announced 4,000 mostly UK-based job losses

tasks.prompt: Why is credibility with bond markets important to the government's Budget choices?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לקשר בין אמון המשקיעים, עלות גיוס החוב, אינפלציה, גירעון והצורך בכרית תקציבית.
expected_points: Investors' confidence affects the interest cost of government borrowing
Higher yields make servicing public debt more expensive
More debt costs reduce money available for other priorities
The government may then face tax rises, spending restraint or larger deficits
Rupert Harrison said the UK is treated as guilty until proven innocent on fiscal responsibility
Credibility was weakened by the Truss mini-Budget and delayed deficit reduction
Inflation remaining above the Bank of England's target also matters
A fiscal buffer can reassure markets that the government can absorb shocks

tasks.prompt: Summarise the chancellor's economic message, the market challenge and the reactions to his plans.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לסכם את מסר הצמיחה, הלחצים בשוק החוב, עמדת האופוזיציה והמומחים, ואת הקרן לצפון אנגליה.
expected_points: Healey urged confidence and described Britain as resilient and ready for new opportunities
He prioritised growth across every postcode
He would not specify tax or spending decisions before the Budget
Borrowing costs and debt-market volatility intensified pressure on the public finances
He promised fiscal discipline, a buffer and balanced day-to-day spending
Conservatives criticised his failure to rule out tax rises
The IFS questioned how achievable growth in every postcode would be
A market adviser warned that UK fiscal credibility had weakened
Healey announced a £150m fund for innovative northern firms
Opposition figures argued the fund or wider response was insufficient

tasks.prompt: Write a short briefing that evaluates whether Healey's growth plan answers the concerns raised in the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב באנגלית הערכה מאוזנת המבוססת על פרטי הכתבה, להבחין בין הצהרות למדיניות ולציין לפחות יתרון, סיכון ושאלה פתוחה.
expected_points: Identify the goal of spreading growth through devolution and investment
Mention the £150m fund and its £5m-to-£15m investments
Explain how public investment is intended to unlock private investment
Acknowledge high borrowing costs and stretched public finances
Consider the promise of fiscal discipline and a spending buffer
Note uncertainty about tax rises or spending cuts
Assess the IFS warning that growth everywhere is difficult in practice
Consider criticism that £150m may have limited impact
Distinguish optimistic rhetoric from confirmed measures
End with a reasoned conclusion grounded in the article
